title: Challenger Staff Trading Policy (Version 10)
date_approved: November 2018 (Authorised by the Group Risk Committee)

tiers.name: staff
tiers.description: All employees of the Challenger Group including its Key Management Personnel, regardless of Division, and the consultants, directors (including non-executive directors), officers, agents and contractors that act for or on behalf of Challenger Group entities. All specific rules for trading Challenger Securities (Prohibited Periods, pre-trade approval, short term gain, margin lending, net short positions, derivatives and hedging) apply to this whole tier.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Persons with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling Challenger's activities directly or indirectly, per AASB 124, including all directors of Challenger, the CEO and certain of the CEO's direct reports. Distinguished only in that their pre-approval to trade Challenger Securities must be granted by the Committee rather than through the ordinary online process.

tiers.name: Designated Staff
tiers.description: The CEO, CEO Direct Reports and staff nominated by a CEO Direct Report or who by virtue of their role have or may have access to sensitive information about Challenger Securities or products, or about Challenger's trading positions (researchers, those aware of Challenger positions or M&A activity, those making recommendations or decisions on Securities Challenger trades, and those involved in fund management). Distinguished by needing pre-trade approval for Third Party Securities as well, and must sign a Designated Person Form - Acknowledgement and Undertaking.

tiers.name: Non-Executive Directors
tiers.description: Non-executive directors of Challenger Group companies. They are within 'staff' and, as Challenger directors, within KMP for Challenger Securities (so Committee pre-approval applies), but are expressly treated as non-Designated Staff for trading in Third Party Securities.

tiers.name: closely connected persons and entities
tiers.description: Related parties or controlled entities such as an immediate family member, or companies and trusts including self-managed superannuation funds, through which a staff member's ownership of or power over Securities may be acquired. Holdings and powers held through them count as the staff member's personal trading.

definitions.hedging_definition: the hedging of or taking out of derivatives over Challenger Securities are not permitted to be used in relation to any unvested Challenger Securities. For the purposes of this Policy, Challenger Securities are considered vested once the Challenger imposed time and performance hurdles have been satisfied, irrespective of whether a Challenger staff member has opted for a longer period of restriction.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Challenger imposes 'additional periods' from time to time when it is considering matters which may include price sensitive information and/or matters subject to ASX Listing Rule 3.1A; the Company Secretary manages the commencement and end dates and staff communications. The Boards of entities issuing the relevant Challenger Securities may vary the timing of closed periods at any time, and the Board and CEO may require temporary changes to the procedures. Refusal of an approval to trade is final and binding and must be kept confidential.

rules.detail: Derivatives and hedges over unvested Challenger Securities are flatly prohibited because they would distort performance and time hurdles. No venue limit and no approval route within 7.6; only the exceptional circumstances process in part 9 could conceivably reach it.
rules.evidence: Accordingly, the hedging of or taking out of derivatives over Challenger Securities are not permitted to be used in relation to any unvested Challenger Securities.

rules.detail: Securities count as vested once Challenger-imposed time and performance hurdles are met, even if the staff member has elected a longer restriction period, so a self-elected holding lock does not push the shares back into the unvested prohibition; the 7.6.2 gateways and criteria apply.
rules.evidence: For the purposes of this Policy, Challenger Securities are considered vested once the Challenger imposed time and performance hurdles have been satisfied, irrespective of whether a Challenger staff member has opted for a longer period of restriction.

rules.detail: OTC derivatives are expressly within Securities ('derivatives (both over the counter (OTC) and exchange traded)') and Challenger Securities expressly include security specific derivatives, options, CFDs and warrants issued by third parties over CGF. Over vested securities, derivatives are permitted only in three defined circumstances, must not mature in a closed prohibited period, must not have any Challenger Group entity as counterparty, and must go through the pre-trade approval process (Committee approval for KMP).
rules.evidence: once Challenger Securities have vested, derivatives or hedging may be used in relation to those vested Securities in the following circumstances: to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out for the exercise price of options granted by Challenger; to protect the value of the security where the staff member had paid or is required to pay a tax liability in relation to the vested Securities; on a case by case basis with approval from the Committee.

rules.detail: Hedging is banned over any unvested Challenger Securities, with no tier or approval carve-out.
rules.evidence: The use of derivatives over unvested Challenger Securities could distort the proper functioning of these hurdles and reduce the intended alignment between management and shareholder interests. Accordingly, the hedging of or taking out of derivatives over Challenger Securities are not permitted to be used in relation to any unvested Challenger Securities.

rules.detail: Unusually permissive: hedging vested securities is endorsed as encouraging longer term holding. It is allowed only (a) to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out for the exercise price of Challenger options, (b) to protect value where the staff member has paid or must pay a tax liability on the vested securities, or (c) case by case with Committee approval. Two mandatory criteria apply on top: no maturity date falling within a closed prohibited period, and no Challenger Group entity as counterparty. The hedge must also comply with the law and the pre-trade approval process.
rules.evidence: Further, any use of derivatives or hedging over vested Challenger Securities must meet both of the following criteria: the derivative or hedge must not have a maturity date that falls within a closed prohibited period; and neither Challenger nor any member of the Challenger Group can be a counter party to the derivative.

rules.detail: For KMP (all Challenger directors, the CEO and certain direct reports) the pre-approval for any trade in Challenger Securities, including entry into a hedge, must be granted by the Committee (Chair of the Board, CEO and General Counsel and Company Secretary for directors; CEO and General Counsel and Company Secretary for other staff), with the requesting member excluded.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel will require pre-approval to trade in Challenger Securities to be granted by the Committee.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or collar-and-loan is a trade in Challenger Securities (Securities expressly include OTC derivatives and third party derivatives referencing CGF) requiring pre-trade approval outside a Prohibited Period, must not create a net short position, and over plan securities must fit one of the 7.6.2 gateways.
rules.evidence: Trading includes the following: applying for, acquiring or disposing of (or entering into an agreement to do so) any Securities;

rules.detail: The ban is on holding net short positions in Challenger Securities through derivatives or otherwise, framed as a general principle. A conventional collar over shares actually held (long stock, long put, short call) is net long and so is not caught; a naked written call or a put purchased over shares not held would be.
rules.evidence: As a general principle, staff are prohibited from holding net short positions in Challenger Securities through derivative instruments or otherwise.

rules.detail: Securities lending or borrowing is not mentioned anywhere and is not within the definition of trading, which is limited to applying for, acquiring or disposing of Securities and procuring others to do so.

rules.section: Key Terms (Challenger Securities; Securities or Division 3 Financial Products); 7.3; 7.6
rules.detail: CFDs are expressly named in both the Challenger Securities and the Securities definitions, so trading a CFD over CGF requires pre-trade approval outside a Prohibited Period. A short CFD would breach the net short position prohibition, and a CFD held less than three months would breach the short term gain rule.
rules.evidence: It also includes security specific derivatives, options, Contracts for Difference (CFDs) and warrants that may be issued by third parties where the underlying or referenced security is Securities issued by Challenger or any other subsidiary entity.

rules.detail: Margin lending over Challenger Securities is prohibited by default but is expressly approvable by the Challenger Board. This is the only board-level financing consent in the policy and is the gateway for the loan leg of a funded structure. No conditions, process or timeframe for that Board approval are stated.
rules.evidence: Challenger prohibits margin lending over Challenger Securities other than as approved by the Challenger Board.

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over Challenger Securities is not addressed except through the margin lending prohibition in 7.5. The definition of trading does not sweep in encumbrances, so a pledge that is not part of a margin loan is not itself a trade requiring approval.

There is no general prohibition on secured financing; only margin lending over Challenger Securities is restricted, and even that is subject to Board approval. A term loan secured on CGF shares without margin call mechanics is arguably outside 7.5, but the general rule that 'You must not do indirectly what you are prohibited from doing directly' means a bank should assume the Board consent route applies. Notably 7.6.2 positively contemplates a hedge protecting an asset supporting a loan.

Symmetric three month rule in both directions (sell after buy, buy after sell) applied to parcels of Challenger Securities, which by definition include derivatives over CGF. Carve-out only for vesting or exercise of performance rights or options and the subsequent sale of those shares; expressly captures shares taken as short term incentive payment.
rules.evidence: Accordingly, selling a parcel of Challenger Securities after buying within a 3 month period is prohibited as is buying a parcel of Challenger Securities after selling within a 3 month period.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary via the 'Request to trade securities' online form on the Challenger intranet
clearance.evidence: Pre-trade approval is required for all trading in Challenger Securities (except as outlined in section 7.3.2 below). Staff must complete and submit an online request to trade form for Challenger Securities via the Challenger intranet prior to trading ... Approved trades must be placed within 1 business day and complete within 7 days, unless otherwise informed by the Company Secretary.

clearance.approver: The Committee: for directors, the Chair of the Board, the CEO and the General Counsel and Company Secretary (or delegate; the Chair's delegate is the Chair of the Group Risk Committee); for staff other than directors, the CEO and the General Counsel and Company Secretary (or delegates). A conflicted member is excluded.
clearance.evidence: Key Management Personnel will require pre-approval to trade in Challenger Securities to be granted by the Committee. KMP may complete the online request to trade form via the Challenger intranet or contact the Company Secretary directly.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary (for Third Party Securities), following a review of current Challenger trading activity and against the restricted Securities list
clearance.evidence: Pre-trade approval is required for all trading in Third Party Securities for Designated Staff (except as outlined in sections 8.1.1, 8.1.2 and 8.1.3). Pre-trade approval is obtained from the Company Secretary.
Non-Executive Directors of Challenger Group companies are considered to be non-Designated Staff for the purpose of trading in Third Party Securities.

short_term.basis: parcel basis, symmetric: sale within 3 months of a purchase and purchase within 3 months of a sale
carve_outs: vesting or exercise of Challenger performance rights or performance options and subsequent sale of such shares
short_term.evidence: This includes where a staff member elects to receive short term incentive payments by way of Challenger Securities. This does not restrict the vesting or exercise of Challenger performance rights or performance options and subsequent sale of such shares.

exceptions.approver: The Committee, on written request addressed to the General Counsel and Company Secretary or the General Manager, Risk and Compliance
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship such as a pressing financial commitment that cannot reasonably be satisfied otherwise than by selling Challenger Securities or Third-Party Securities;
a court order, court enforceable undertaking, or other legal or regulatory requirement requiring a sale of Challenger Securities or Third-Party Securities;
such other circumstances deemed or considered to be exceptional or extraordinary circumstances by the Committee.

Forced sales or acquisitions as a result of margin lending calls or corporate actions such as takeovers, bonus issues, share splits / consolidations, dividend re-investment plans, non-renounceable rights etc. which do not accommodate personal discretion are not subject to pre-trade approval for Designated Staff.

corporate actions such as takeovers, bonus issues, share splits / consolidations, dividend re-investment plans, non-renounceable rights etc. which do not accommodate personal discretion are not subject to pre-trade approval for Designated Staff.

The Prohibited Periods do not restrict participation in Challenger share, performance options and performance rights plans but do apply in respect of any subsequent trading of Challenger Securities to which Challenger staff become entitled under those plans.

Trading in Challenger Securities which are units in a public superannuation fund or an unlisted managed investment scheme including mFunds do not require pre-trade approval. The other requirements of this Policy (including the General Trading Rules) apply.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No express price-trigger guidance, but 7.6.2 imposes a timing constraint on the hedge itself: 'the derivative or hedge must not have a maturity date that falls within a closed prohibited period'. A collar must therefore be dated to mature outside the 30 June and 31 December closed periods, and a structure whose maturity or early termination could be pulled into a closed period is non-compliant.

exemption_authority: Part 9 (Exceptional Circumstances): a staff member not in possession of inside information who wishes to trade in Challenger Securities or Third Party Securities in a way that would otherwise breach the Policy (including trading during a Prohibited Period) needs specific prior written approval. The written request goes to the General Counsel and Company Secretary or the General Manager, Risk and Compliance, with supporting evidence, and is decided by the Committee, which may impose conditions in its absolute discretion including execution and settlement time limits and post-trade reporting. Separately, the Challenger Board may approve margin lending over Challenger Securities (7.5), and the Board and CEO may require temporary changes to the procedures (1).
jurisdiction_overlays: Entities and Divisions operating outside Australia must consider local rules; where local rules are more stringent they always prevail, and any direct conflict must be notified to the Policy Owner before local policies are implemented

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging over vested securities expressly permitted
bespoke_clauses.clause: once Challenger Securities have vested, derivatives or hedging may be used in relation to those vested Securities in the following circumstances: to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out for the exercise price of options granted by Challenger; to protect the value of the security where the staff member had paid or is required to pay a tax liability in relation to the vested Securities; on a case by case basis with approval from the Committee.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is one of the few ASX policies that positively contemplates hedging vested shares, and the first limb even contemplates a hedge protecting an asset that supports a loan; a collar over vested shares can therefore be approved on a case by case basis by the Committee.

bespoke_clauses.clause: neither Challenger nor any member of the Challenger Group can be a counter party to the derivative.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank writing the collar must not be a Challenger Group entity, which is straightforward for a third party bank but excludes any Challenger-issued structured product.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the derivative or hedge must not have a maturity date that falls within a closed prohibited period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar's expiry must be scheduled outside the 30 June to results and 31 December to results closed periods, and rolling or early termination must be planned around dates that can shift when the Boards vary closed period timing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Challenger prohibits margin lending over Challenger Securities other than as approved by the Challenger Board.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg is not an absolute bar as it is in most ASX policies: the Challenger Board can approve margin lending over CGF securities, so a funded collar turns on obtaining that Board approval alongside Committee approval of the hedge.

bespoke_clauses.clause: As a general principle, staff are prohibited from holding net short positions in Challenger Securities through derivative instruments or otherwise.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar must be sized no larger than the shares actually held, since an over-hedged position or a written call in excess of the holding would create a net short position.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Shares, securities, interests in a managed investment scheme including mFund units, options, stock specific derivatives, derivatives (both over the counter (OTC) and exchange traded), warrants, contracts for difference (CFDs) ... It also includes security specific derivatives, options, Contracts for Difference (CFDs) and warrants that may be issued by third parties where the underlying or referenced security is Securities issued by Challenger.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so both collar legs written by a bank are Challenger Securities requiring pre-trade approval and subject to the Prohibited Periods.

bespoke_clauses.topic: prohibited periods framed around quoted securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: There are periods throughout the year during which Challenger staff are not permitted to trade in Challenger Securities which are quoted on a relevant stock exchange irrespective of whether or not they are in possession of inside information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Prohibited Period wording is expressed by reference to quoted securities, but 7.6.2 assumes derivatives are subject to closed periods, so a bank should not rely on an argument that OTC legs escape the blackout.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approved trades must be placed within 1 business day and complete within 7 days, unless otherwise informed by the Company Secretary. Once the approval lapses, re-approval to trade will be required.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar must be placed within one business day of approval and completed within seven days, though the Company Secretary can vary this, which is likely necessary for a negotiated OTC structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval to trade can be granted or refused in the Company's absolute discretion, without providing any reasons. An approval to trade may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. Any refusal to trade is final and binding on you, and you must keep that information confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval to enter, roll or unwind the collar can be withdrawn between pricing and execution, with no appeal and no reasons given.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You must not do indirectly what you are prohibited from doing directly.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A term loan secured on CGF shares that is economically a margin loan, or a synthetic short achieved through combined legs, will be treated as caught even if the label differs.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced sale carve-out sits in the third party rules
bespoke_clauses.clause: Forced sales or acquisitions as a result of margin lending calls or corporate actions ... which do not accommodate personal discretion are not subject to pre-trade approval for Designated Staff.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only forced-sale relief appears in section 8 (Third Party Securities) and is expressed for Designated Staff, so it is unclear whether a lender's enforcement sale of CGF shares in a Prohibited Period is protected.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A staff member's ownership or power in Securities may be acquired through closely connected persons and entities including a related party or controlled entity such as an immediate family member or companies and trusts including self-managed superannuation funds.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar through a family trust, SMSF or controlled company is treated as the staff member's own personal trading and needs the same approvals.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Version 10, Date of Version November 2018, Review of Policy Due by November 2019.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The lodged policy is dated November 2018 and was due for review in November 2019, so the bank should confirm no more recent version has superseded these unusually permissive hedging provisions.

summary: Challenger is unusually accommodating and a funded collar over vested shares is genuinely possible, but only with two separate consents. Section 7.6.2 expressly permits derivatives and hedging over vested Challenger Securities, including to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan, and otherwise on a case by case basis with approval from the Committee (Chair, CEO and General Counsel and Company Secretary for directors; CEO and General Counsel and Company Secretary for other staff), while section 7.5 prohibits margin lending over Challenger Securities 'other than as approved by the Challenger Board', so the loan leg requires Board approval. The structure must satisfy the two mandatory criteria that no Challenger Group entity is a counterparty and that the hedge does not mature within a closed prohibited period, must not create a net short position, must be entered outside the 30 June and 31 December closed periods and any additional period, and must go through pre-trade approval with the trade placed within one business day and completed within seven days. Nothing may be hedged while unvested, though securities count as vested once Challenger's own hurdles are met even if the executive has elected a longer restriction. The three month short term gain rule and the anti-avoidance principle that staff must not do indirectly what they cannot do directly mean the tenor must exceed three months and a loan structured to avoid the margin lending label would still be treated as caught.
